newsitem.title: USA: Privatizing Mass. buses risks federal funds -union.
newsitem.headline: Privatizing Mass. buses risks federal funds -union.

text.p: A union representing Massachusetts bus drivers on Wednesday said that the U.S. government had told the state that its privatization plan might put it at risk of losing federal transit funds.

Massachusetts has given private contractors until November 15 to bid on its 159 bus routes, a move that would put approximately 2,000 bus drivers out of work. The state gets about $8 million of operating assistance from Washington for transit.

The union quoted a letter from the U.S. Department of Labor that gave the Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority until October 8 to explain how it plans to comply with a federal law designed to protect jobs.
Section 13(c) of the Federal Transportation Act is intended to ensure that agencies take all possible cost-savings measures before laying off workers or cutting wages and benefits, said the union.
Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority has asked a court to issue a declaratory judgment saying that this provision does not apply.
The union interpreted the letter from the federal Department of Labor as supporting its position that this section applies, which it said could force the Authority to drop its privatization plan.
"Basically, you're talking about scrapping the whole project if Section 13(C) applies," said John Laughlin, a spokesman for the union.
The Authority noted that it has yet to actually privatize any of its bus routes, adding that the union might turn out to be one of the groups that bid for them.

"We believe right now that the inquiry is premature and that the service has not yet been completely contracted out. And Local 589 still has a chance to compete for the work. And we hope that they do," said Philip Puccia, the chief of staff.
